standard.title: 21 CFR Part 11 — electronic records and electronic signatures, mapped to what the package can carry
standard.scope_note: Five clauses of Subpart B/C. This is not a Part 11 compliance checklist: Part 11 binds the person who uses the system to keep records, and the controls it names (validation, access control, training, written policy) live in that person's quality system. Rows were chosen because they name something a record layer can either demonstrate or plainly not.

rows.reason: The probe recomputes every evidence digest and names the entry whose bytes changed: 2/2 on the clean package, and on the tampered one it reports the mismatch instead of passing. That is the 'ability to discern invalid or altered records' half, demonstrated rather than asserted. The validation half - IQ/OQ/PQ, a validation plan and report accepted by the user's quality unit - is the user's work, and a library cannot perform it for them.

Events are computer-generated, time-stamped, append-only and carry the actor that made them; the verifier checks that actor against the recorded principals (its actor allow-list), and the seal makes a later insertion visible, so a change does not silently obscure what was recorded before. Two limits stay honest: the actor check's own test coverage is thin, so this row's probe demonstrates the time-stamped trail rather than the authorization; and the retention period is a records policy the user sets, which a format can preserve but cannot decide.
carrier: per-event actor field checked by the verifier's actor allow-list against recorded principals

rows.reason: Two of the three elements are present and checkable: when the seal was applied, and what it means (the verdict it asserts). The printed name of the signer is not: the package carries a key identity, not a person's name, and mapping a key to a named individual is the user's identity-proofing step under 11.100(b).
carrier: signer key identity in the manifest

rows.reason: Each AEE observation record carries its own DSSE signature over that record's PAE, and records.record_verified checks it against the consumer's pinned key rather than the keyid the record happens to carry. The probe copies record 0's signature list onto record 1 and record 1 stops verifying; delete record 1's signatures and it stops verifying; record 0 is unaffected either way. That is the 'cannot be excised, copied, or otherwise transferred' test, run on a vendored upstream conformance vector instead of on a demo of our own. Not covered: the physical execution of a handwritten signature (pen on paper). Once such a signature has been executed to an electronic record its bytes are record content and inherit the same binding, but the pen-and-paper step is outside any software layer.
carrier: AEE observationRecords: one DSSE signature per record
records.record_verified pins the signer key and never trusts the carried keyid

rows.reason: This is change control over the system's own documentation - procedures, revision history, approval of revisions. It belongs to the user's quality system, and no record layer can supply the procedure it asks for.
